blocks.title: Standard enthalpy change of reaction
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy of a reaction, delta Hr, is the enthalpy change when stoichiometric amounts of reactants in their standard states react together completely to form products under standard conditions.
For example, hydrogen and oxygen forming one mole of water: H2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) gives H2O(l), delta Hr = -286 kJ per mol.

blocks.prompt: If the equation for water formation is doubled to 2H2 + O2 giving 2H2O, what is delta Hr, and why?
blocks.explanation: It doubles to -572 kJ, because the enthalpy change of reaction refers to the stoichiometric amounts written in the equation; twice the amounts give twice the heat.

items: Delta Hr: the enthalpy change for the stoichiometric amounts of the equation reacting completely under standard conditions; H2 + 1/2 O2 giving H2O(l) is -286 kJ per mol.
